title: Improved Recovering-Security Bound for CTR-DRBG
summary: A contrived universal-hash example makes a factor-p loss inherent for the generic analysis, but a stronger recovering-security bound for concrete CTR-DRBG using CtE's structure remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{CTR\text{-}DRBG}$, a generic counterexample based on a contrived universal hash function shows that treating $\mathrm{CtE}$ only as a universal hash can inherently incur a factor-$p$ loss when one of $p$ inputs is selected adaptively; this counterexample does not establish that $\mathrm{CTR\text{-}DRBG}$ itself has inferior recovering security. Prove a strong recovering-security bound for $\mathrm{CTR\text{-}DRBG}$ that improves on this generic factor-$p$ loss by exploiting concrete structure of $\mathrm{CtE}$ beyond its universal-hash property.

scope.domain: Cryptographic security bounds for NIST CTR-DRBG and the concrete CtE construction.
assumptions: One of p inputs is selected adaptively
parameters: p, the number of inputs among which one is selected adaptively
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a strong recovering-security bound for CTR-DRBG can improve on the generic factor-p loss by exploiting concrete CtE structure beyond its universal-hash property.

progress.summary: The source gives a contrived universal-hash counterexample showing that the factor-p loss is inherent under that abstraction, while noting that this does not show inferior recovering security for CTR-DRBG itself. It points to exploiting concrete CtE structure as the route to a better bound.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., Security Analysis of NIST CTR-DRBG
